title: 3.6.13 Lab: Nested-Structure Mutation
description: Show that a spread copy is only one level deep: change a nested array inside the copy and the original still changes. Then fix it with a deep copy. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Copy the outer object with spread
steps.instructions: Create an object called student that contains a nested array (for example, a list of scores). Make a shallow copy called shallow with the object spread syntax: a new object with the same keys.

steps.title: Change the nested array inside the copy
steps.instructions: Push a new value into the nested array of shallow. Then log both shallow and student. Notice student changed too, because a shallow copy still shares the nested array.

steps.title: Make a deep copy instead
steps.instructions: Use structuredClone to make a copy called deep that goes all the way down. Push a DIFFERENT value into the nested array of deep, then log both again to prove student is now untouched.

requirements.title: outer object copied with spread
requirements.description: Code copies an object with the spread syntax. Help: 3.6.10 (Defensive Copying: [...] and {...})
requirements.hint: Make a copy with spread in braces. It is a new object, but anything nested inside is still shared.

requirements.title: nested array pushed into
requirements.description: Code pushes into a nested array through a property access. Help: 3.6.9 (Side Effects and Copies)
requirements.hint: Reach the nested array through the copy's property and call .push on it.

requirements.title: structuredClone used
requirements.description: Code calls structuredClone for a deep copy
requirements.hint: structuredClone(object) copies all the way down, including nested arrays and objects.

requirements.title: objects logged
requirements.description: Code calls console.log. Help: 3.6.9 (Side Effects and Copies)
requirements.hint: Log the copy and the original after each change, so you can see whether the original moved.

requirements.title: the shallow copy shares the nested array, the deep copy does not
requirements.description: shallow.scores matches student.scores (they are the same array), deep.scores is different from it, and the output shows the arrays. Help: 3.6.9 (Side Effects and Copies)
requirements.hint: Push into shallow.scores and student.scores changes too. Push a different number into deep.scores and student.scores stays as it was.

checks.expr: JSON.stringify(shallow.scores) === JSON.stringify(student.scores) && JSON.stringify(deep.scores) !== JSON.stringify(student.scores) && output.filter(l => l.includes('[')).length >= 4
checks.fail: Make student, a spread copy called shallow and a structuredClone copy called deep. After pushing into each copy, the shallow copy matches student (they share the array) and the deep copy differs. Print the arrays after each change.
